text:
- chief complaint: the patient reports right and left hand and wrist pain, numbness, and tingling, mostly at night, for several months.
- history of present illness: gradual onset of nocturnal hand numbness and pain, sometimes waking the patient with the hand "asleep," relieved by shaking. Symptoms involve all fingers, most prominently the thumb and index finger, with occasional little-finger numbness. Left side is worse. Symptoms are linked to repetitive, heavy manual labor (landscaping). Alcohol use is one or two beers on weekends. No known history of rheumatoid arthritis.
- physical examination: grip strength weaker on the left; decreased sensation over the thumb side of the fingers; positive Tinel's sign bilaterally (wrist tap elicits tingling in the fingertips); heart and lungs unremarkable.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: nocturnal numbness and tingling in fingers, hand pain, left-hand weakness, dropping objects, nocturnal waking with hand numbness.
- new medications prescribed or changed: ibuprofen 600 mg every six hours.
- follow-up instructions: reduce repetitive hand activities for a couple of weeks, delegate heavy work, wear a wrist splint, follow up in two weeks; EMG ordered; possible surgical referral if no improvement.
